joe_cust: Hey team — our embedding vectors suddenly differ between Hosted and our Private deployment for the same model+input. Hosted returns length 1536 but Private returns 1024. This started after the weekend. Any ideas?

maria_support: Sorry you're hitting this, @joe_cust. Can you paste the request you're sending (sanitized token)? Also which model ID and exact input text?

joe_cust: Sending sanitized curl below. Model is `open-embed-xxl-v1`. Input is just: "how to reset my password?"
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "open-embed-xxl-v1", "input": "how to reset my password?"}'
```
Response (Hosted): `{"data": [[...1536 numbers...]]}`
Response (Private): `{"data": [[...1024 numbers...]]}`

maria_support: Thanks. Can you confirm whether the Private endpoint is behind Dedicated routing or pure Private (on-prem)? Also any recent config changes to batching or quantization?

joe_cust: Private is on-prem (customer-managed) but connected to Redwood control plane. We did a kernel update last week, but that was infra team. No intentional batching changes from our app.

jun_sre: Paging in case this is a runtime fallback. Quick checklist: 1) confirm model artifact version (SHA) on both sides, 2) check if the Private runtime fell back to a smaller backbone (quantized variant), 3) inspect request headers for `X-Model-Variant` or `X-Deployment-Tag`. @alex_eng can we see model metadata?

alex_eng: I checked registry: `open-embed-xxl-v1` has two published variants: `xxl-fp16-1536` and `xxl-8bit-1024` (the latter is a config we added for low-memory Dedicated). They should be pinned by model SHA, but there's a routing policy that can fallback to the low-memory variant when capacity/cold-starts or certain rate limit violations occur.

joe_cust: Interesting — we didn't expect auto-fallback for Private. How would that be triggered?

alex_eng: Two common triggers: 1) runtime reports OOM during loading and signals fallback; 2) routing policy sees that the auth-tier or quota exceeded and redirects to cheaper variant. We log both events to the control plane. Can you share request IDs from your Private calls?

joe_cust: One Private request id: `req_prv_202403040843_9f3a`. Hosted id: `req_hst_202403040843_d12b`. I can attach full logs if needed.

maria_support: Thanks — @sre-bot, can you pull the control-plane event trail for `req_prv_202403040843_9f3a`?

sre-bot: control-plane: found events for req_prv_202403040843_9f3a -> [2024-03-04T08:43:12Z] model-load-error: "OOM while allocating KV cache"; fallback_variant: "xxl-8bit-1024"; route: private-cluster-07.

jun_sre: That matches. OOM on Private triggered fallback to the 1024 variant. Two follow-ups: 1) why did it OOM now (memory pressure/driver update?), 2) why didn't the client get a clear status code/notice instead of silent dimension change?

alex_eng: For (1) ops-bot will show recent node changes. @ops-bot any infra events for private-cluster-07 around that time?

ops-bot: infra: node-reboot on private-cluster-07 at 2024-03-04T08:40:55Z; kernel-driver: nv_driver_1.2.4 -> 1.2.6 applied; memory pressure alerts 08:41-08:44Z.

maria_support: For (2) this is a UX gap — currently fallback is silent for embeddings endpoints to preserve availability. We should at least emit a warning header `X-Embed-Variant-Fallback: from=1536;to=1024` and include a non-2xx field in diagnostics. I'll file an internal ticket.

joe_cust: Appreciate the root cause. Short term, we need reproducible steps so we can confirm: what should we check on our side to avoid surprises?

jun_sre: Repro steps for Private cluster owners: 1) check node memory and driver versions `kubectl describe node private-node-XX` 2) verify model artifact SHA: `redwoodctl models get open-embed-xxl-v1 --cluster private-cluster-07` 3) inspect recent control-plane events `redwoodctl events --request req_prv_202403040843_9f3a` 4) if you want embedding shape enforcement, set `X-Strict-Embed-Dims: 1536` header — server will 412 if it can't serve that dim (note: not yet widely documented).

joe_cust: Trying header now. Private request with header resulted in HTTP 412 + body: `{"error":"Requested embedding dimension 1536 not available; served 1024"}` — perfect for our integration tests.

maria_support: Great. Action items: - Support: document `X-Strict-Embed-Dims` in troubleshooting guide. - Eng: add fallback warning header and a short note in API changelog. - SRE/Ops: investigate kernel driver OOM regression and schedule node rolling update if needed. Assigning owners: @maria_support (docs), @alex_eng (api header), @jun_sre (infra).

joe_cust: Thanks folks, milestone for us is to avoid silent shape changes. We'll keep `X-Strict-Embed-Dims` in CI for now. :thumbsup:

maria_support: Following up — I'll send a short repro checklist and the docs PR link in this thread once live.

alex_eng: I'll add the fallback header in the next runtime patch and include a migration note. ETA 2 business days.

jun_sre: I'll run a node health sweep on private-cluster-07 and report back with suggested patch window.

joe_cust: Acknowledged. Leaving logs here if anyone needs them: `/mnt/logs/req_prv_202403040843_9f3a.log`

maria_support: Thanks — closing the ticket once docs + header are live.
